model_annotation: This pie chart, titled “Error rate for slots” from the paper “Continual Dialogue State Tracking via Reason-of-Select Distillation,” visually represents the distribution of error rates across different dialogue slots. The chart is divided into 13 distinct slices, each labeled with a slot name and its corresponding percentage. The largest slice is “date,” accounting for 19.30% of the total, followed by “from” at 17.00% and “to” at 14.50%. Other significant slices include “genre” at 13.50%, “name” at 5.20%, and “size” at 4.20%. Smaller segments include “time” (4.10%), “location” (3.80%), “intent” (3.80%), “destination” (3.00%), “city” (2.60%), “class” (2.40%), “range” (2.20%), “type” (2.00%), “beds” (1.30%), and “passengers” (1.10%). Each slice is color-coded, though the specific colors are not described in the data, and the chart includes percentage labels directly on the slices as well as a legend that maps each slot to its respective segment. The slices appear to be arranged in descending order of size, with the largest segment at the top right and progressively smaller segments moving clockwise.
